title: Drop expired messages from the outbox in place

blocks.text: Partner messages wait in an outbox until they are sent, and each has a deadline after which it is no longer worth sending. Every few seconds the sender calls `dropExpired(now)` before it sends the rest. The batch sender keeps its outbox in an `ArrayList`; the live sender, whose list other threads read while it sends, keeps it in a `CopyOnWriteArrayList`. Both go through the same `Outbox` class, and its callers keep their own reference to the list, so the expired messages must leave that very list.

Finish `dropExpired(long now)` in `src/main/java/practice/Outbox.java`: drop every message whose deadline is at or before `now`, keep the others in order, and return how many were dropped. It has to work on both senders' lists. About three lines.

cases.says: before any deadline, nothing is dropped and the outbox keeps its order
a message whose deadline is exactly now is dropped and the others keep their order
several expired messages spread through the outbox are all dropped, without an exception
two expired messages next to each other are both dropped
an outbox kept in a CopyOnWriteArrayList drops its expired messages as well

origin.section: Change a Collection During Its Own Walk Only Through the Iterator, or with removeIf

concepts: During a walk, elements are removed through the iterator or with removeIf; the collection's own remove in a for-each throws or skips, and a forward index loop skips the element after each removal.
